prompt: A labelled teaching adaptation of the page 83 tyre example supports a treaded wheel on a driven road roller with a small external wheel drive and brake. Drive applies wheel torque and shows the contact traction reaction at the anchored support. Wet supplies a thin water film and traces its escape through the tread grooves, comparing grip with the dry trial without claiming every wet tyre loses all traction. Brake applies external axle braking torque while the roller remains driven and reverses the tangential reaction. See-through shows tread blocks, grooves, tyre, wheel and road contact. The roller, supports, water supply and torque input are teaching fixtures. Do not add a hydraulic brake system, invented tyre internals or automatic aquaplaning at every speed.

title: Parachute
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Friction
prompt: A labelled teaching adaptation of the page 83 parachute uses a light payload, flexible canopy and suspension lines in a transparent still-air drop column. Drop releases the externally packed specimen and lets it accelerate downward. Open externally releases the canopy restraint after sufficient downward speed, inflates the canopy and shows drag initially exceeding weight so descent slows. Follow tracks the subsequent approach to steady descent as drag and weight balance. See-through shows canopy, lines, payload and restraint, with air motion, drag, weight and speed as overlays. The column, external release and slowed display time are teaching fixtures. Do not invent an automatic opening mechanism or assert that a short fall has reached terminal speed before the forces actually balance.

title: Clutch
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Friction
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the pages 84 and 85 coil-spring car clutch connects an externally hand-driven flywheel to a transmission shaft with a small external resisting load. Engage releases the pedal so the coil springs clamp the friction-lined clutch plate between flywheel and pressure plate and bring the output up to speed. Release presses the pedal, moves the fork, thrust bearing and thrust pad against the release levers, and withdraws the pressure plate. Take up slowly partially releases the pedal so friction accelerates the loaded output before full engagement. See-through exposes the pictured plates, cover, coil springs, release levers, fork, thrust bearing, pad and shaft. Heat is an energy-loss overlay. Do not substitute a diaphragm spring or force incompatible speeds after full lock.

title: Synchromesh

title: Oil rig
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Friction
prompt: A labelled scale teaching adaptation of the page 87 land oil rig lowers a rotating drill pipe and tricone bit into a replaceable layered rock specimen. Drill rotates the pipe and lets the three toothed cones turn against the rock under applied axial weight, crushing and grinding it. Circulate pumps drilling mud down inside the pipe, through the bit and up the outside annulus to cool the bit and carry cuttings upward. Filter separates cuttings at the surface and returns mud to the supply tank while circulation continues. See-through traces the pipe bore, annulus, bit cones, mud path, pump, tank and filter as a functional circuit without invented pump or filter internals. Heat and flow are overlays. No oil-production pump, blowout-preventer mechanism or automatic rock repair is claimed.
